_method: preview_strategy_report, 1h anchor. Each transform is checked against its OWN trajectory slots in the same table, so no external data is needed and no sampling drift can creep in between the operand and the result. Where bars:'closed' was used, the trajectory slots were additionally diffed against data/audit/candles_btc_1h_battlegrid.json.
_why: docs/19 verified the METRICS (RSI, ATR, SMA, EMA) against the textbook. It did not touch the TRANSFORMS, which are the layer omega's whole column algebra sits on. Before this audit exactly one of the seventeen - spread - had ever been checked against its stated formula.

verified.stated: slots = last window non-null base values; trend = compare(first, last)
verified.check: CLOSE trajectory window=5 bars=closed on BTC returned 78740, 78924, 78971, 78729, 78996 - identical to the last five CLOSED candles (19:00 through 23:00 on 2026-08-24). Confirms both the slot semantics and that bars:'closed' really does exclude the forming bar.

verified.check: BTC: |78996-78740| / (184+47+242+267) = 256/740 = 0.3459 -> rendered 0.35. SOL: a perfectly monotonic run, |99.05-96.50| / (0+0.99+0+1.56) = 2.55/2.55 = 1.000 -> rendered 1.00. The degenerate case landing exactly on 1.0 is the strong half of this.
BTC VOLUME window=4 bars=closed, using exact candle volumes: 1356.15 / (1315.32+1002.39+845.79+1356.15) = 0.30005 -> rendered 0.30. SOL: 448.4K / 894.9K = 0.5011 -> rendered 0.50.

First attempt used FUNDING_RATE, whose eight slots were all 0.0013 - a degenerate series that would match any central-tendency statistic, so it proved nothing. Re-run on OI window=6, which varies: SOL (441.3+443.6+443.6+458.7+492.2+519.1)/6 = 466.42 -> rendered $466.4M. DOGE 429.6/6 = 71.6 -> $71.6M. AVAX 95.5/6 = 15.92 -> $15.9M.
verified.result: exact on a varying series - it is the arithmetic mean, not a median

verified.check: Six columns across BTC and SOL, all consistent under interval arithmetic on the displayed operands. EMA5/EMA13 and rate/atrPct pin exactly; rate/chg24h only to 0.73pp because the denominator sits near zero. See docs/19.

verified.stated: ordinal(base among the ranked universe, by the chosen ordering)
verified.check: ATR_PCT ranked hi and lo across five coins. Ordering is monotone in the underlying value in both directions, and rank_hi + rank_lo = 79 = universe + 1 for EVERY coin (AVAX 36+43, BTC 48+31, DOGE 25+54, ETH 40+39, SOL 29+50). That identity holds only for a true tie-free ordinal over a fixed universe, and it holds five times out of five.
verified.result: exact - and proves hi/lo are exact inverses over 78 coins

operationalFindings.finding: rank is scoped to the whole active market, not your coin selection
operationalFindings.evidence: The response carries rankScopingNote: 'Rank columns reflect the full active market, not the previewed coin selection - a coin may show a rank higher than the number of rows shown.' Ranks rendered as n/78 while only 5 coins were selected.
operationalFindings.consequence: Every cross-sectional family - carry-factor, xs-momentum, and the rest - ranks against 78 coins regardless of how many the strategy actually reads. A 'top decile' gate means top of 78, not top of your shortlist.

operationalFindings.finding: rank does NOT repaint intra-bar, unlike every other indicator
operationalFindings.evidence: Header meaning states: 'the standing as of the last close, unchanged until the next one.'
operationalFindings.consequence: A documented exception to cookbook trap 18. Rank columns are stable within the bar; value/trajectory/aggregate columns are not.

operationalFindings.evidence: In the same render, offset=0 drifted from the cached recomputation while offset=3 matched to the cent. An offset of 1 or more lands the window on closed bars, which no longer move.
operationalFindings.consequence: A second escape from cookbook trap 18, alongside bars:'closed' - and this one keeps the forming bar out of the window while still reading a metric that has no bars parameter of its own.

platformDefects.finding: Two columns whose headers collide RENDER, but both vanish from conditionColumns.
platformDefects.repro: One section, CLOSE trajectory window=6 bars=closed, SMA20 value offset=3, SMA20 value. The table renders 9 data columns and the header row reads '... | close_trend | SMA20 | SMA20 |' with two different values ($78,215.50 and $78,469.20). conditionColumns for that section lists SEVEN outputs - close_t5 through close_trend. NEITHER SMA20 appears.
platformDefects.why: offset is not part of the header name, so any two columns differing only by offset collide. The same applies to any other parameter the namer ignores.
platformDefects.cost: The agent still SEES both values as table text, so the table looks correct. But a condition referencing 'SMA20' has no column to bind to. Combined with BG-6 - a null read is FALSE, never UNRESOLVED - a gate written against that header fails silently and reads as a real negative.
platformDefects.control: SMA20 alone, without the offset twin, appears in conditionColumns normally with lt/lte/gte/gt/between. So the metric is conditionable; the COLLISION is what removes it.
platformDefects.suggestedFix: Either disambiguate the header when offset is set (SMA20_off3, as trajectory already does with _t3), or reject the section with REPORT_COLUMN_HEADER_COLLISION. Rendering a column that cannot be referenced is the worst of the three options.
